notes.subject: plate
notes.text: White plates with a noticeable red block near the left side; the blue EU strip is only sometimes present. Serbian plates nearly always have the strip.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Generation 3 cars never show an antenna, which is true almost nowhere else; Serbia is mostly antenna-free but sometimes has one.

notes.subject: coverage
notes.text: All Generation 4 coverage is smallcam: mounted low, with a big round blur and a small protrusion at the front.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Two types: a thin rounded one and a wedge, both white with red or white reflectors on a black panel. The wedge matches Croatia's.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: A-profile guardrails with red reflectors. Serbia uses B-profile.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Direction signs are typically yellow, with town names in both Latin and Cyrillic. Only Serbia also does both.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Warning signs normally have a yellow fill, where most of Europe uses white. Greece does the same.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Cyrillic script with Ѓ and Ќ unique to this language; Љ, Њ and Џ are shared only with Serbian. Most other signs are fully Cyrillic.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: "Greek lamps" on utility poles, also found in Greece and Serbia.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Relatively dry grassland with small hills and scattered trees.

notes.subject: coverage
notes.text: Generation 3 coverage is sparse: some highways plus eight main cities with in-city coverage.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Large apartment blocks almost guarantee you are in the capital, by far the biggest city.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Poster obituaries on poles vary by city; those in Kumanovo are the only ones with a thick light blue border.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Prilep obituaries are vertical and black, with a border that does not go fully around.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: Black and yellow striped kerbs suggest Strumica; around roundabouts they suggest Tetovo.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The only large city lying right next to a lake.
